featured.title: Berlin Election: Which Ballot Your Passport Gets You
featured.summary: Berlin votes on Sunday 20 September. German citizens vote for the parliament and district assembly; eligible EU citizens vote for the district assembly. Online postal-vote applications closed on 15 September, but the normal in-person deadline is Friday 18 September at 15:00. Completed postal votes must reach the district office by Sunday at 18:00.
featured.alt: The Abgeordnetenhaus von Berlin on Niederkirchnerstrasse, the former Prussian Landtag, a long neoclassical facade with columns and flags flying in front under a blue sky
featured.label: Current: Berlin election

miniPosts.title: Oktoberfest in Berlin 2026: What Is Actually On
miniPosts.summary: Berlin has several Oktoberfest-style events in 2026, but none is Munich's city-defining Wiesn. Compare confirmed dates, places, transport and the event that best fits your trip.
miniPosts.alt: Illuminated Prater Garten sign at dusk on Kastanienallee in Prenzlauer Berg, Berlin's oldest beer garden

miniPosts.title: Mould in Berlin Flats: When Airing Dries the Room and When It Soaks It
miniPosts.summary: An open window can dry a Berlin flat in winter but bring moisture in during some summer hours. Ten years of Berlin-Tempelhof weather readings show when airing helps, and how a cold wall can reach mould-friendly humidity even when the room feels dry.
miniPosts.alt: A window in a Berlin flat standing wide open on a bright day, looking across to Altbau facades on the far side of the street

miniPosts.title: Berlin Museums Closed for Renovation: What Is Shut and What to See Instead
miniPosts.summary: The Pergamonmuseum has been shut since October 2023, Museum Berggruen since 2022, and the Zeughaus is a building site with no announced reopening. Here is what is actually closed in Berlin right now, which reopening dates you can trust, why the Ishtar Gate is on a far longer clock than the 2027 headlines suggest, and what is genuinely worth doing instead this week.
miniPosts.alt: The Ishtar Gate reconstructed inside the Pergamonmuseum, a blue glazed brick gateway with rows of golden animals

miniPosts.title: Berlin Public Transport for Tourists: Tickets, Zones, Prices and Validation
miniPosts.summary: Berlin public transport uses one shared ticket system for U-Bahn, S-Bahn, tram and bus. This local guide covers zones, prices, validation, BER airport trips, and the EUR 60 fine.

posts.summary: Need a toilet in Berlin? This tourist guide shows where to find public toilets, what they cost, where the free options are, and when stations, malls, or the Berliner Toilette app help.

posts.title: Berlin Rent Increase: Which of the Four Limits Actually Stops the Letter
posts.summary: The Berliner Mietspiegel 2026 put the median net cold rent at 7.71 euro per square metre, and the rent letters built on it are landing now. Four separate limits decide whether yours holds up, and for most Berlin tenants the famous 15 per cent is not the one doing the work.
posts.alt: A Gruenderzeit apartment building on Hermannstrasse in Berlin-Neukoelln, with red brick and stucco ornament above the ground floor windows and blue sky reflected in the panes
